# Appeal of Denied Prior Authorization — Request for Reconsideration

**Morgan Lawson**
Member ID: W441316160
[My mailing address]
[My phone number]

**Date:** [Date I am sending this letter]

**To:** Aetna Better Health of West Virginia
Member Complaint and Appeal Unit
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]
Fax: 859-425-3379

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-19 — Reference number POC-CBB1679293-79812**
**Member:** Morgan Lawson | **Member ID:** W441316160
**Service denied:** Lower back disc surgery / decompression, CPT 63030
**Governing policy:** *Spinal Surgery: Laminectomy and Fusion (CPB 0743)* — https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/700_799/0743.html

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for the lower back decompression surgery (CPT 63030) requested by my surgeon, Dr. Duval, MD, orthopedic surgery. The notice dated 2026-08-19 states that the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before the requested surgery. I am asking the plan to reconsider, because the records that were already submitted show conservative treatment that meets the plan's own published requirements.

I am relying on the plan's policy *Spinal Surgery: Laminectomy and Fusion (CPB 0743)*. Below I quote that policy and show where my records match it.

## 1. The plan's conservative therapy requirement

The policy states:

> "Member has failed at least 6 weeks of conservative therapy Footnote1 * (unless there are indications for waiver of requirements for conservative management, noted below); and"

My records document 12 weeks of supervised physical therapy, from 2026-04-13 to 2026-07-06, with 16 visits completed. That is twice the minimum period the plan itself sets out, and it did not resolve my symptoms.

## 2. The plan's requirements for what conservative care must include

The policy states:

> "Conservative measures must be recent (within the past year) and include the following non-surgical measures and medications unless one or more of the requirements for waiver below are met: patient education; active physical therapy (in-person as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy); medications (NSAIDS, acetaminophen, or tricyclic antidepressants), and (where appropriate) identification and management of associated anxiety and depression."

Matching my records to that language:

- **Recent (within the past year):** My physical therapy ran from 2026-04-13 to 2026-07-06, and my corticosteroid injection was on 2026-05-25 — all within the year before the denial.
- **Active physical therapy (in-person):** Supervised physical therapy including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility, 16 visits over 12 weeks.
- **Medications (NSAIDs):** NSAIDs for 8 months, with inadequate relief. I also had a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-25 that gave only about 4 weeks of partial relief.

## 3. The plan's proof requirement for physical therapy

The policy states:

> "The member should participate in physical therapy for the entire required duration of conservative management (six weeks or three months, depending upon the indication for surgery). Physical therapy needs to be confirmed either by the actual PT notes, or by documentation in the member claims history."

My physical therapy is documented in the physical therapy discharge note, which is the form of confirmation the policy asks for. My 12 weeks of therapy satisfies either duration named in that sentence. If the plan did not receive the discharge note, I ask that it be requested and reviewed before this appeal is decided; I am also submitting it with this letter.

## 4. The other criteria in the same policy are also supported by my records

The policy states:

> "Member has signs or symptoms of neural compression (radiculopathy, neurogenic extremity claudication, myelopathy) associated with the levels being treated; and"

I have radicular pain into my right calf, and my examination showed positive provocative testing on the affected side with a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level.

The policy states:

> "Advanced imaging studies (CT or MRI) indicate central/lateral recess or foraminal stenosis (graded as moderate, moderate to severe or severe; not mild or mild to moderate), or nerve root or spinal cord compression, at the level corresponding with the clinical findings; and"

My MRI of the lumbar spine on 2026-06-23 shows an L4-L5 disc extrusion with **severe** right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root. That is severe stenosis, plus nerve root compression, at the level that matches my symptoms and my exam findings.

The policy states:

> "Advanced imaging studies are required prior to any spinal surgery. The imaging should be performed within the past year, or after the onset of the current constellation of symptoms or any relevant surgical procedures, whichever is sooner."

My MRI was performed on 2026-06-23, within the past year.

The policy states:

> "For purposes of this policy, Aetna will consider the official written report of advanced imaging studies (e.g., CT, MRI, myelogram). If the operating surgeon disagrees with the official written report, the surgeon should document that disagreement."

The findings above are from the official written MRI report submitted with the request.

The policy states:

> "Member's activities of daily living are limited by symptoms of neural compression;"

I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes, and I have had 18 months of progressive lower back pain that is not relieved by rest.

The policy states:

> "Medical records must document that a physical examination, including a neurologic examination, has been performed by or reviewed by the operating surgeon."

My records document a physical examination with positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level. My operating surgeon is Dr. Duval, MD, orthopedic surgery, and he has documented that this procedure is needed.

The policy states:

> "All other reasonable sources of pain and/or neurological deficit have been ruled out, including but not limited to significant pathology at other spinal level(s) on the advanced imaging radiology report that is/are not part of the surgical request resulting in incomplete surgical planning; and"

The official MRI report identifies the L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and L5 nerve root compression, and my clinical findings correspond to that level. If the plan believes some other source of my pain has not been addressed, I ask that it identify specifically what it has in mind so my surgeon can respond.

## 5. Two points I am asking the plan to clarify

First, the policy contains a waiver provision that begins:

> "The requirement for a trial of conservative measures may be waived in the following situations indicating need for urgent intervention: Spinal cord compression (this does not include nerve root compression); Stenosis causing cauda equina syndrome;"

I understand this list continues with further conditions that are not reproduced in the excerpt available to me, and I am not claiming a waiver — I completed conservative care. I mention it only to note that the policy contemplates more circumstances than the ones I can see.

Second, the policy contains a requirement about diabetes:

> "For elective laminectomy (cervical, lumbar, and thoracic), if member is diabetic, their HbA1c should be less than 8 percent within 3 months prior to surgery, unless there is an indication (e.g., myelopathy, cauda equina syndrome), severe weakness (graded 4 minus or less on MRC scale) or progressive weakness, or an associated infection/tumor and/or acute fracture."

The clinical summary submitted for me does not identify diabetes as a condition of mine. My records do note that I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker. If the plan relied on this criterion, I ask that it say so, and I will supply [lab result, if applicable].

## What I am asking for

The denial rests on conservative care. The plan's own policy sets that requirement at six weeks of conservative therapy, including in-person active physical therapy and medications, documented by PT notes. My records show 12 weeks and 16 in-person supervised physical therapy visits, 8 months of NSAIDs, and an injection that gave only temporary partial relief — all within the past year, all in the submitted packet.

I respectfully ask Aetna Better Health of West Virginia to:

1. Overturn the denial dated 2026-08-19 (reference POC-CBB1679293-79812) and authorize CPT 63030;
2. If the denial is upheld, tell me in writing exactly which criterion of *Spinal Surgery: Laminectomy and Fusion (CPB 0743)* was not met and what specific documentation would satisfy it; and
3. Have this appeal reviewed by a physician with training in spine surgery.

I am submitting this appeal using Aetna's Member Complaint and Appeal Form (available in my account at aetna.com, under complaints, grievances and appeals), by fax to 859-425-3379 or by mail to the appeal address printed on my denial letter. Per the notice I received, my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice — **by 2027-02-15** — and I am sending it well before that date. I can also be reached by phone at 1-800-872-3862 or the number on my card if the plan needs anything further from me.

Thank you for taking a fresh look at my records.

Sincerely,

**Morgan Lawson**
Member ID: W441316160
[Signature]
[Date signed]

**Enclosures:** [Physical therapy discharge note, 2026-04-13 to 2026-07-06] · [MRI lumbar spine report, 2026-06-23] · [Office/exam notes from Dr. Duval, MD] · [Medication and injection records] · [Copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-19]

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
